one_liner: Zero-copy wire format for existing .proto schemas. In-place field reads beat Protobuf parse-then-read ~25-50x and FlatBuffers ~2x.
what_it_does: YaFF keeps your .proto as the schema but replaces Protobuf's varint wire encoding with a flat, mmap-able buffer that you read in place, with no parse step. A protoc plugin (called through yaff_generate() in CMake) generates read-only view types in a protoyaff:: namespace, with accessors named like Protobuf's (foo(), has_foo(), foo_size(), *_case()). yaff::Serialize<T>(proto_msg) builds a buffer, yaff::ReadMessage<T>(ptr) returns a view over it, and ParseTo/ParseMessage convert back to a Protobuf object. It is meant to run alongside Protobuf and be adopted one module at a time, not to replace it: views are immutable, so any edit goes through a Protobuf round trip.
how_it_is_fast: Field offsets are computed at code-generation time (a constexpr FLAT_OFFSETS table per message). A Flat-layout read is one bounds compare against a 2-byte header plus one unaligned memcpy load. Values are stored XORed with their default, so unset fields are zero bytes, and nested messages are reached through 32-bit relative offsets. The layout structs are declared [[gnu::packed, gnu::may_alias]] and the generated accessors [[gnu::pure]], so GCC and Clang can eliminate repeated accessor chains such as root.intermediate().leaf().x(), which FlatBuffers users have to cache by hand. The default 'dynamic' layout switches each message at runtime between this Flat layout and a Sparse layout that finds fields through a per-message offset table (close to FlatBuffers' vtable approach); the Flat path is marked as the likely branch.
when_to_use: A C++ service already uses Protobuf and a hot path parses whole messages only to read some fields. YaFF keeps the .proto and removes the parse: 25.99 ns vs 1383.74 ns to read 100 uint64 fields.
Dense, mostly populated messages of fixed-width scalars read repeatedly from cache-resident data (the ~2 KB hot working set). There the Flat layout stays within about 1.2-3x of a raw C++ struct.
Read-mostly blobs (precomputed features, documents, cached responses) that you write once and then mmap or pass around and query in place, where you control both writer and reader.

An alternative to FlatBuffers when you want one .proto source of truth and Protobuf's schema-evolution rules. In the authors' runs Flat is ~2x faster on flat reads and ~1.45x faster on cold random access.
Small fixed-shape records (coordinate pairs, key/value entries) pinned to LAYOUT_FIXED and inlined into arrays for single-load, struct-like access, as long as that schema never changes.
when_not_to_use: Buffers from untrusted sources. There is no verifier (unlike FlatBuffers' Verifier), so reading a malformed or hostile buffer is undefined behavior.

Size-sensitive storage or network links with sparse or small-valued data. YaFF has no varints, so Protobuf with small values is smaller in every measured case: at 50 fields and 5% density, Flat is 294 B vs 14-32 B for Protobuf.
Non-C++ consumers. Only C++ is supported today and other language bindings are on the roadmap. CI covers only Linux with GCC 13 and Clang 17, so MSVC is untested.

Schemas that rely on proto2 extensions (their values are dropped), groups (unsupported), field numbers above 8190 (these must be remapped), large maps (stored as a key-sorted array searched with binary search) or keeping unknown fields when converting back to Protobuf (they are lost on ParseTo).
Code that needs in-place mutation or a stable API. Views are read-only, the only release is v0.1.0 (pre-1.0), and generated code must match the runtime's exact version or it fails to compile.

integration.form: static lib (header-only runtime yaff::core + static yaff::proto + protoc-gen-yaff code generator)
integration.dependencies: Protobuf >= 5.26 (libprotobuf at runtime, protoc for code generation); CMake >= 3.20; Conan 2 optional (the package is built into a local cache, not published on ConanCenter)
integration.min_toolchain: C++20, CMake 3.20; CI tests GCC 13 and Clang 17; the published benchmarks used Clang 20.1.8
integration.platforms: CI covers only Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 24.04). The headers have MSVC fallbacks (pragma pack, with no may_alias or pure), but MSVC is not tested. Byte order is not documented: values are read with native-order memcpy and never byte-swapped.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Read views are const, noexcept overlays on immutable bytes and keep no state, so concurrent readers of one buffer look safe. yaff::Serializer is a mutable builder that cannot be copied or moved, so use one per thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — reuses the .proto and mirrors Protobuf's getter names, but the wire format is new and not binary-compatible with Protobuf, the types live in a separate protoyaff:: namespace, views are read-only, and you convert explicitly with yaff::Serialize and ParseTo

gotchas: The headline numbers need the Flat layout. Removing a field with plain `reserved` (or deleting it) drops its type, and the dynamic layout then falls back to Sparse, which runs at about FlatBuffers speed (60.11 vs 54.81 ns for 100 fields). To stay on Flat, mark the field `[deprecated = true]` or restate its type in the `reserved_fields` option.

YaFF treats some changes as breaking that Protobuf calls conditionally safe: changing a default, widening int32 to int64, or turning a singular field into a repeated one. Every enum is open, including proto2 enums that Protobuf treats as closed.

The fast direct-write API (generated SerializeFoo(ys, ...)) is documented as internal. Its arguments are positional, so removing a middle field can silently shift values onto other fields of the same type. The recommended path builds from a Protobuf object, so writes still pay for Protobuf message construction.

The buffer must outlive every view and string_view taken from it. Choosing Flat or Sparse for dynamic messages is manual today (Serializer::EnforceDynamicAlternative, default Flat); automatic, data-driven selection is still on the roadmap. Presence detection for float/double fields was fixed on 2026-09-23 (PR #18), so use a recent commit.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose YaFF over ProtoCache, the other zero-copy format driven by .proto files, when field-read latency matters more than data size and you want Protobuf's own evolution rules; ProtoCache aims at compact cached data and changes some schema semantics. Choose SBE for fixed-layout, multi-language financial messaging with XML schemas, and Fory when serialize/deserialize throughput matters more than reading fields in place.
verified_claims_summary: In the authors' google/benchmark suite (Clang 20.1.8, Release build with no -march, AMD EPYC 7713), reading all 100 uint64 fields from a prebuilt buffer took 25.99 ns with YaFF's Flat layout, 54.81 ns with FlatBuffers 24.12.23 and 1383.74 ns with Protobuf (version unpinned, >=5.26); the Protobuf time includes ParseFromString into a fresh message on every iteration. On a 3-level hierarchy with a ~512 MB cold working set the lead shrinks to 1.9x over Protobuf and 1.45x over FlatBuffers (206.64 vs 387.48 vs 300.13 ns).
status_note: The Yandex project is active (last commit 2026-09-23) but very young: repo created April 2026, one v0.1.0 release, pre-1.0 API, no GitHub issues filed yet; it is Apache-2.0 (GitHub shows NOASSERTION, but LICENSE is the standard Apache text) and builds with CMake or as a local Conan 2 package.
